author: original (NevaIB)
title: Geometric sequences and series

points.text: General term of a sequence with constant ratio
Sum of the first n terms; sigma notation

bigPicture: A geometric sequence multiplies by the same ratio each step. It models any repeated percentage change, so it links directly to finance (1.4) and exponential functions (2.9).

keyIdeas.cue: General term of a geometric sequence?
keyIdeas.answer: u_n = u₁ r^(n − 1), where r = u_(n+1)/u_n is constant.

keyIdeas.cue: Sum of the first n terms?
keyIdeas.answer: S_n = u₁(r^n − 1)/(r − 1) = u₁(1 − r^n)/(1 − r), r ≠ 1. Pick the version with a positive denominator.

keyIdeas.cue: How do you model repeated percentage change?
keyIdeas.answer: Growth by p%: r = 1 + p/100. Decay by p%: r = 1 − p/100. Check whether the starting value is u₁ or the value 'after 0 steps'.

keyTerms.def: r = u_(n+1)/u_n, the same for every pair
the factor 1 ± p/100 for a p% change

workedExamples.title: First term over 10 000
workedExamples.prompt: 2, 6, 18, … Find the first term greater than 10 000.

practice.prompt: A geometric sequence has u₂ = 12 and u₅ = −96. Find r, u₁ and S₆.
commonErrors: r = 2 (losing the sign of the cube root)
Sign slip in the sum formula

practice.prompt: A runner runs 5 km in week 1 and increases the distance by 10% each week. Find the distance in week 8 and the total over the first 8 weeks.

assessmentNote: AA SL external exams: Paper 1 without a calculator and Paper 2 with a GDC, both written answers in sections A (short) and B (extended); no multiple choice. Practice prompts here are original and are not predictions of exam questions.
